findings.text: non-blocking: _identity re-implements lead_decisions._request_identity at reckon/crew/lead_decisions.py:171 in the same terms, and the decision write at lost_session_work.py:349 bypasses lead_decisions.record_decision and validate_decision, duplicating the owner of the decisions store.

non-blocking: an adopt answer accepts any non-empty session string, so the lead can move a record to another lost or unknown session even though the plan says a live session; nothing checks liveness before the pointer mutation.
non-blocking: the docstring cites plan sections §5 and §4, a plan-label reference in source that the naming rule forbids; the test should name the mechanism instead.

non-blocking: the landing case calls skip_lost_session_landings directly and never runs _land_deliveries, so a regression that dropped the reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:2282 wiring or its recorded reason would leave the suite green.

non-blocking: crew_decision_answer catches OSError, ValueError and TypeError but not the CrewError that runs.read_pointer raises for a vanished run, so an adopt of a run that disappeared surfaces as a traceback rather than the decision_error JSON the sibling handlers emit.
